purpose: Three independent isolated rainforest bird chirps, replacing the old voice-like low coos on phones
notes: Synthetic bird sound design, not a field recording or species-certified example. Each master is independent. Final browser assets select one brief middle-register chirp with silence around it. No mammal-like coo or hoot.

assets.title: Rainforest rising chirp
assets.role: One isolated short rising tropical forest bird chirp
assets.prompt: TrackType: SFX, One solitary small tropical rainforest songbird gives one short clear soft wheet chirp, a delicate flute-like rising whistle with a quick clean ending. Recognizable natural bird chirping in a middle register around 1800 to 2500 Hz, not piercing or shrill. The single chirp lasts half a second, surrounded by quiet outdoor air and long silence. No repeated notes, no call train, no chorus, no coo, hoo, hoot, throat, grunt, groan, mammal, ape, owl, pigeon, human voice, insect, rain, music or instruments. Length: 5 seconds.

assets.title: Rainforest falling whistle
assets.role: A separate isolated short descending rainforest bird whistle
assets.prompt: TrackType: SFX, A single shy tropical forest bird makes one brief soft descending sweet chirp, a clear airy twee whistle that bends down and stops. A natural short bird call in the middle register around 1500 to 2200 Hz, lightly woody but clearly whistled, never low or throaty. Only one half-second bird phrase with silence before and after. No continuous song, no repeated chirping, no cooing, hooting, mammals, ape voice, owl, pigeon, human voice, insects, weather, music or instruments. Length: 5 seconds.
